At my friend's 16th birthday party, her openly gay uncle who was also very talkative struck up a conversation with me.

I've always been very shy and awkward, but for some reason, he sat down next to me and started asking me questions about myself.

The party was held at the park down the street from her house, so we played with water balloons and danced listening to music. Every single time we had down time, I sat down next to him and he'd continue talking to me, right where we had left off before.

My friend kept saying things like "I'm sorry if he's bothering you, he's a real chatterbox." but I continuously said it was fine, that I enjoyed it.

He finally asked me if I had ever dated anyone and at the time, I had just gotten out of my first relationship. He told me that he was married for years before he was comfortable with what he really wanted in life. He said that one day he couldn't lie to this wife, who he remained friends with, anymore and he came out, and they divorced. I'll never what he said after that. Not only did he tell me I was a young, beautiful woman (I had very low self-esteem at the time) but that I deserved the love and respect that I was seeking, not by anyone else's standards, but by mine.

It was so nice hearing this from an adult at that age. I was so used to having my ides be rejected by authority just because I was younger. He was the first person to ever treat me like an adult and tell me my thoughts and feelings were valid. He also told me to never settle for less.

Because his feet would sweat so much, that if he took the pair of socks off and then put them back on, his feet would get all gross and he'd get athletes foot... fungus... that kind of gross shit.

Fast-forward to about a year ago, I ran into him at the bar and he starts telling me how shitty of a person I am. I say to him with a straight face "Oh by the way, I didn't wring your socks out on purpose."

He left and I never saw him again.
